title: One Purchase, Start to Finish
tagline: Follow a single order from empty bin to paid invoice — and catch what goes wrong on the way.

cast.storyRole: spots the shortage and raises the requisition
approves the quantity, picks the vendor, sends the PO
runs the 3-way match before anyone gets paid

seo.description: Run one real purchase end to end at a furniture plant: requisition, approval, vendor choice, PO, receiving, and the 3-way match before payment.

glossary.definition: An internal raised hand: a request for approval to buy. Dale raised one when Rack 14 ran low on steel tube — it never goes to any vendor.
The binding document sent to the vendor: what, how much, at what price, by when. Once acknowledged, both sides are committed.
Comparing PO, goods receipt, and invoice before paying. If the three don't agree, Nadia's stamp stays in the drawer — and so does the money.

lines.text: Rack 14 is down to eight days of 25-millimeter steel tube, and Crestline needs six to deliver. If we sit on this, we'll be counting hours instead of days.
I'm raising a requisition now — Ray sees this before lunch, not before Friday. The Fairview line doesn't wait.

payload.prompt: The Fairview chair line bends about 650 kg of tube a day. Crestline delivers in 6 days. How much should Ray approve?

choices.label: 2,000 kg
choices.implication: About 3 days of cover after arrival
choices.feedback: That covers the gap only if nothing slips. One late truck and the Fairview line stops anyway.

choices.label: 4,500 kg
choices.implication: About 7 days of cover after arrival
choices.feedback: Covers the 6-day lead time plus a buffer for a late delivery, without freezing a month of cash sitting as steel.

choices.label: 9,000 kg
choices.implication: Two weeks of cover — and half of Rack 14
choices.feedback: Safe, but that's cash sitting on a shelf and rack space you don't have. Over-ordering is a cost too, just a quieter one.

payload.teachingPoint: Order quantity is a cash-versus-risk decision: cover the lead time plus realistic slippage, not your anxiety.

payload.prompt: Three vendors can supply 25mm tube. It feeds the flagship line — a critical material. Who gets the order?

options.name: PrimeSteel Direct
options.note: No quality audit on file for a critical material.

payload.feedbackCorrect: Right. On the material that feeds your flagship line, a proven vendor at $1.85 beats an unaudited one at $1.62 — the 23-cent saving is smaller than the cost of one stopped line.
payload.feedbackWrong: Tempting price — but an unverified vendor on a critical material is how production lines stop. The saving doesn't survive one bad batch of tube.
payload.teachingPoint: Vendor selection prices in risk, not just dollars per kg. Critical materials earn stricter rules.

payload.intro: Ray drafted the PO between two phone calls. Check it before it goes out.

fields.label: Unit of Measure
fields.explanation: Tube is bought by weight, not length. A vendor shipping 4,500 meters would deliver a completely different quantity than 4,500 kg.

fields.label: Delivery Address
fields.explanation: Bay 5 is finished goods. Raw material trucks that arrive there get turned away — and the six-day clock restarts.

payload.teachingPoint: A PO error becomes everyone's error downstream — receiving, accounts, and the vendor all inherit it.

payload.prompt: The truck backs into Bay 3 and 4,500 kg checks in clean. Nadia opens the match: what should Crestline's invoice line total be?
payload.teachingPoint: The 3-way match starts with arithmetic anyone can do — and catches errors nobody else will.

questions.prompt: Crestline's invoice arrives showing 4,700 kg. The GRN says 4,500 kg. What does Nadia do?

options.text: Pay it — the difference is small
Hold payment and query the mismatch with the vendor
Edit the GRN to 4,700 so the documents agree

questions.explanation: The match failed, so payment stops until the documents agree. Editing the GRN to force agreement is how companies pay for goods that never arrived.

questions.prompt: Which document committed Nexara to the price?
questions.explanation: The PR asks internally; the GRN records arrival. The PO is the binding commercial document both sides committed to.

takeaways: Procure-to-pay is one chain: PR → Approval → Vendor → PO → GRN → Invoice match → Payment.
Every document exists to catch a specific kind of error before it becomes money.
Vendor choice on critical materials is a risk decision, not a price decision.
When the 3-way match fails, payment stops — the documents are made to agree by investigation, never by editing.
